quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay within the posted speed limit.
Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to finish the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the legal speed limit. Pass only when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the controls are in the same places as on your bike.
Take it straight out on the highway.
Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle on the road, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a controlled area to get used to the bike.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of the stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best protection. They should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:

options.text: Is always on the left side.
Is always on the right side.
Depends on the situation.

questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on what the road and traffic conditions require.

questions.question: Before riding with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Have your passenger wait until after you start the engine to mount. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Before riding, check the clutch. A good clutch should feel:

options.text: Loose and rough.
Tight and smooth.
Loose and smooth.

questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:

options.text: Help in most situations.
Improve steering.
Cause control problems.

questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause loss of control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce accident risk by:

options.text: Not looking ahead for hazards.
Avoiding turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.
Being visible to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Reduce collision risk by being visible, using clear signals, keeping space between you and other vehicles, watching ahead, and spotting hazards early. Be ready to react to any danger.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle:

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake means you may not build the skill to use the front brake properly in an emergency stop.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid busy traffic areas.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To avoid danger while riding, always look far ahead on the road. Watch for hazards early so you have time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do these actions separately, one after the other. Never brake and swerve at the same time because this can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and do not use the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars tightly and keep your motorcycle going straight. Only brake if you are sure which tire is flat. Slow down and exit the road once it is safe.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Any soft material.

questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar tough material. This gives you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: Motorcycles may pass on the right:

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear road space.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on the grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear road space.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear, unobstructed road space. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you control a motorcycle in a turn?

options.text: Speed up through the turn.
Slow down before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.explanation: To turn safely, slow down before the turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Lean your body and press the handlebars to lean the motorcycle. Gently speed up as you come out of the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly.
Be uncomfortable.

questions.explanation: Your riding jacket should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement or makes you uncomfortable.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the distance between you and the vehicle ahead should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.

questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield can protect you from:

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your face in a crash. It also protects you from everyday hazards like rocks from other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow.
Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
Be fully extended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press the handlebars without having to stretch.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you position your motorcycle in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon, which is also dangerous.

questions.question: What happens if you grab the front brake hard or slam on the rear brake?

options.text: The brakes can lock up.
It is the best way to stop in an emergency.
It is the best way to slow down on wet streets.

questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or slamming the rear brake can cause the brakes to lock. Locked brakes make it hard to control your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Lanes shift ahead.
Yield to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead becomes slippery when it rains.

questions.question: How should you adjust your speed when riding at night?

options.text: Ride at the same speed as during the day.
Ride slower than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on roads you don't know well. Slower speed gives you more time to see and avoid hazards in the dark.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Wear gloves while riding to improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.
